title: Metric Synapse Evaluator: derive inference KPIs and anchor OTLP metrics to traces
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's inference platform emits a mix of Prometheus metrics, OTel metrics, and spans. Customers and SREs need per-request derived KPIs (token_latency, decode_time, kv_cache_hit, cold_start_flag, per-route token-cost attribution) that are currently expensive or impossible to compute downstream because: (a) instruments are spread across host-level exporters, (b) trace->metric linkage is lossy, and (c) high-cardinality labels (model_id, route, tenant) explode Prometheus cardinality.

Goal:
Implement a lightweight "Metric Synapse Evaluator" that performs deterministic enrichment and KPI derivation for inference requests at the telemetry onramp. The component should: (1) attach a stable request identity (request_id/trace_id) to metric envelopes, (2) derive per-request KPIs and convert them into bounded-cardinality Prometheus/OTel metrics and histograms, (3) compute KV cache hit rate and cold-start signals, (4) provide a fallback path for missing spans (best-effort anchoring), and (5) expose configuration to trade off accuracy vs cardinality for Dedicated/Private customers.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: agent-side enrichment (sidecar or light process on inference node), central synapse aggregator for tenant-level heavy enrichments, schema definitions for derived KPIs, dashboards and SLO alerts, rollout/feature-flag, end-to-end tests and perf benchmarks.
- Out of scope: rewriting model runtime to emit new metrics (we will use hooks + adapters), long-term storage design for derived metrics (handled by metrics backend teams).

Design decisions and rationale:
1) Hybrid approach: agent-side lightweight enrichers + central synapse service. Rationale: per-request enrichment must be low-latency and colocated for accurate KV/cache metrics. Central service performs label canonicalization and expensive derivations for sampled traffic only.
2) Request identity: prefer trace_id when available; otherwise synthesize a stable request_id using (node_id, timestamp_bucket, nonce). Using trace_id enables direct span->metric correlation in dashboards.
3) Cardinality controls: derive a low-cardinality fingerprint for model variants (model_fingerprint) and expose a configurable label_whitelist per tenant. Default behavior will drop free-form labels and map them to coarse buckets.
4) KPI types: gauge for kv_cache_hit (0/1), summary/histogram for token_latency.decode and token_latency.total with fixed buckets aligned to existing SLOs, counter for token_cost. All derived metrics include request_id and model_fingerprint for correlation but request_id is marked as high-cardinality and automatically sanitized before exporting to Prometheus (kept only in stable KV store for trace linking).

Telemetry contract (initial):
- kpi.infer.token_latency_ms{route, model_fingerprint, tenant, bucket} (histogram)
- kpi.infer.decode_ms{route, model_fingerprint, tenant} (summary)
- kpi.infer.tokens_emitted_total{route, model_fingerprint, tenant} (counter)
- kpi.infer.kv_cache_hit{route, model_fingerprint, tenant, hit} (gauge 0/1)
- meta.request_anchor{request_id, trace_id, model_fingerprint, node_id} (OTel resource/metric to enable lookups)
Rollout plan:
1) Prototype in staging: implement sidecar enrichment on a subset of dedicated nodes. Validate correctness by comparing derived KPIs to ground-truth traces.
2) Canary: enable on 1% of hosted traffic behind feature flag. Monitor CPU/memory overhead, metric cardinality, and alert noise.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% / 50% / 100% with automated rollbacks if tail-latency or cardinality thresholds breached.

Acceptance criteria:
- Derived KPIs present in Prometheus/OTel with the agreed names and buckets.
- Trace-to-metric anchoring works for 99% of sampled traces in staging.
- CPU overhead of agent-side enrichers < 2% p99 per node under synthetic load (bench).
- Cardinality growth within the configured tenant limits; default config does not increase Prometheus label cardinality by >15% on average.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for schema transformations and label canonicalization.
- Integration tests with sidecar + central synapse in staging cluster.
- Backfill comparison job: compute KPIs from raw traces and compare to synapse-produced KPIs to detect drift.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How long to retain request_id -> metric mappings for post-hoc queries? (short retention reduces storage; longer retention simplifies debugging). Proposal: 7 days by default, configurable per tenant.
- Should request_id be exported to Prometheus at all? We will avoid exporting high-cardinality request_id to Prometheus; instead use a small TTL KV store that maps request_id to trace_id for lookups from the Console.

Security & privacy:
- Default sanitization removes any tenant-specific PII from labels.
- Feature gated for Private deployments to allow custom KMS-backed storage for anchor mappings.

Observability / dashboards:
- New dashboards: "KPI Synapse Overview" (per-tenant KPIs, enrichment success rate, agent overhead), "Request Anchor Health" (fraction of metrics with anchors, anchor miss rate), and "KV Cache KPI" (cache hit rate vs token_latency).
- SLO alerts: enrichment-failure-rate > 1% over 5m, derived-kpi-delta (against trace-ground-truth) > 5% for 30m.

Implementation tasks (high-level):
- sidecar: lightweight C++/Go binary to subscribe to local OTel/Prometheus instruments -> produce enriched envelopes (ENG-823457 - placeholder for subtask)
- synapse: central service to canonicalize labels and do sampled heavy derivations (ENG-823458)
- console: dashboard panels and debug UI to resolve anchors (ENG-823459)
- e2e tests, perf harness, and rollout scripts (ENG-823460)

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Metric+Synapse+Design
- Perf benchmark PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1532
- Prototype sidecar draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1601

Notes:
This ticket is intentionally scoped to telemetry enrichment and KPI derivation. If the initial rollout shows unacceptable cardinality growth, follow-up work will implement adaptive sampling and histogram sketching in the synapse central service.
